title: Gretchen Whitmer Rejects Michelle Obama's Pessimism, Says America Is Ready for a Female President
snippet: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer pushed back against claims that American voters aren't ready for a female president, hinting that a Democratic governor—potentially a woman—could win the White House in 2028.
content:
Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer offered a firm defense of female leadership on Sunday, directly disputing former First Lady Michelle Obama's assertion that American voters are still not ready to elect a woman to the presidency.

Speaking on NBC News' Meet the Press, the high-profile Democratic governor expressed strong confidence in the party's bench of executive leaders heading into the 2028 cycle. When asked directly by moderator Kristen Welker whether a female candidate could be the best choice to defeat potential GOP nominees like Vice President JD Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Whitmer offered a straightforward answer: 'I do.'

Leaving the Door Open for 2028

Whitmer's remarks came in response to widely publicized comments made by Michelle Obama, who suggested that the electorate remains resistant to putting a woman in the Oval Office. Whitmer, however, argued that Democratic state executives are uniquely positioned to compete aggressively on the national stage regardless of gender.

While Whitmer previously walked back statements ruling out a 2028 presidential bid, she did not dismiss the possibility on Sunday. With her gubernatorial term ending in January, she indicated that any decisions about her political future will come after taking time off to evaluate her options.

'When I exit office, I'm going to take a little time off and figure out what I want to do next,' Whitmer told Welker, noting that she learned long ago to 'never say never' when it comes to seeking higher office.

Defending Allies on the Campaign Trail

Beyond national politics, Whitmer used her appearance to weigh in on key gubernatorial contests across the country, aiming sharp criticism at Republican businessman Vivek Ramaswamy over a controversial ad aired in Ohio. Ramaswamy's campaign recently launched a spot featuring the estranged mother of Democratic nominee Dr. Amy Acton calling her daughter a 'liar.'

Acton, a former state public health official who was removed from her mother's custody as a child following allegations of sexual abuse by her stepfather, has received strong support from national Democrats amid the fallout. The ad drew widespread condemnation from both Democrats and Republicans, including GOP Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio.

Whitmer labeled the campaign tactic 'abhorrent,' warning that such attacks create additional barriers for survivors seeking public office or help. She stressed the importance of electing leaders like Acton who focus on delivering results for working families rather than engaging in personal smears.
